Are you our new growth hacker? Join Orifarm at the intersection of data, analytics, and business development. You will turn complex market insights into growth opportunities, strengthen portfolio decisions, improve efficiency, and help expand access to affordable medicines across Europe

About the job

As our Portfolio Intelligence & Analytics Manager you will build and maintain a structured portfolio intelligence capability that identifies, evaluates, and prioritizes external growth opportunities across European markets.

In this role, you will translate market intelligence, competitive insights, and analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for Business Development, Portfolio Management, and senior stakeholders.

Your contributions will improve the speed, quality, and consistency of portfolio decision-making, enabling Business Developers to focus on high-potential opportunities and value-creating partnerships.

Your key responsibilities:

• Own and continuously develop the portfolio intelligence capability within Business Intelligence

• Build and maintain a structured pipeline of relevant licensing and development opportunities in close collaboration with key stakeholders

• Establish analytical frameworks and scoring models for consistent opportunity assessment and prioritization

• Monitor European pharmaceutical markets, competitors, pipelines, portfolio trends, and emerging opportunities

• Provide analytical and decision support across Business Development (Rx & OTC), including opportunity assessments, business cases, and portfolio prioritization

• Apply analytics, automation, AI, and digital tools to improve the scalability and quality of the portfolio intelligence capability

• Support broader Business Intelligence activities, including dashboards, reporting, forecasting, and ad hoc analyses

This role requires on-site presence at our headquarters in Odense twice a week.

Who are you?

We are looking for a commercially minded professional with demonstrated expertise in market intelligence and a strong track record of turning complex data into actionable business insights. Experience in the pharmaceutical industry is a significant advantage, particularly within Portfolio Support, Generics, Business Development, Portfolio Management, Market Intelligence, or pharmaceutical consulting. You hold a master’s degree in Business Analytics, Economics, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Life Sciences, or a related field.

You know how to connect analytical findings with portfolio priorities and growth opportunities. You can assess markets, competitors, pipelines, strategic fit, risks, and commercial potential, then communicate your conclusions through compelling data visualizations and decision-ready presentations.

In addition, we envision that you bring:

• A can-do attitude and a team-oriented approach

• A curious, proactive mindset and a strong motivation to solve business problems through data

• Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to navigate complexity and turn it into clear, practical recommendations

• Fluency in English. A Nordic language is a plus

• Experience with the Power Platform is an advantage

Who are we?

As part of Business Intelligence, you will join a small, ambitious team working closely with key stakeholders across Business Development in Rx and OTC and with other relevant functions. You will work in a dynamic, international environment with a supportive, feedback-oriented culture where knowledge sharing and collaboration are part of how we succeed.

Why should you join Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are 2,300 employees united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, enabling our employees to shape their professional development. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

Join Orifarm if you are curious, ambitious, and ready to accept the challenge of bringing more affordable medicine to millions of people.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

AFTERMARKET MANAGER

TriVision is on a growth journey, and we are in the process of expanding our position in the market. For that, we are looking for a new Aftermarket Manager with responsibility for our Service department, our aftermarket business and customer support that keeps our vision systems running at full performance in the field. If you thrive with great responsibility for service operations, customer relationships and continuous improvement of our aftermarket offering – and you're not afraid to open a terminal and write a bit of code yourself – we have the role for you right here.

You will work with the organization to build a strong, proactive service setup, develop our aftermarket revenue (spare parts, service agreements and upgrades) and ensure our customers get fast, competent support. You will be a key point of contact for our customers, handling incoming calls and e-mails and making sure their issues are solved quickly and professionally. Because our vision systems combine hardware with advanced software, you will also get close to the technical core of our solutions – diagnosing issues, building small tools and scripts, and working with our developers to solve problems at the source.

Your areas of responsibility

You will lead and develop the Service department and be the driving force behind our aftermarket strategy. Specifically, you will:

-       Manage and priorities the daily service tasks and the service technicians handling installation support, troubleshooting and maintenance at customer sites.

-       Have personnel management responsibility for the Service department – including staffing, development, one-on-ones and the day-to-day motivation and wellbeing of your team.

-       Be a direct point of contact for customers by phone and e-mail, handling enquiries and support cases and solving their problems quickly and professionally.

-       Own the aftermarket business – service agreements, spare parts sales and upgrade opportunities – and identify ways to grow this area.

-       Act as an escalation point for complex technical and software-related support cases, including remote diagnostics on our vision systems.

-       Write and maintain scripts and small tools (e.g. in Python or similar languages) that support diagnostics, service reporting and internal workflows.

-       Explore and apply AI tools to make service and support more efficient, e.g. for faster troubleshooting, case handling and internal knowledge sharing.

-       Collaborate closely with the software and hardware development teams to feed field experience back into product improvements.

-       Implement and continuously optimize processes to secure documentation, approvals and full delivery of service commitments.

-       Build and maintain long-term relationships with customers and sub-suppliers involved in service and support.

Professional competencies required

You hold a relevant technical education – for example within electronics, mechanical, production or software engineering – or you have equivalent experience from a similar role in the automation, machine vision or industrial technology industry.

You are comfortable with coding and can read, write and debug scripts (Python or similar) to solve practical problems – you don't need to be a professional software developer, but you're not intimidated by code and enjoy using it as a tool. You also have a genuine interest in AI and how it can be used practically to streamline service, support and diagnostics.

You have experience with technical service, support or maintenance, ideally including personnel management responsibility for a team or a service function. You are used to handling direct customer contact by phone and e-mail and enjoy solving customers' problems. Experience with spare parts sales, service agreements or other aftermarket business is an advantage, as is knowledge of the food and packaging industry.

Personal profile

You are service-minded and thrive when you can make customers succeed with our technology. You take ownership naturally and genuinely enjoy people management – motivating, developing and creating a good everyday life for your team – whether you already have managerial experience or have the clear potential and drive to take on the responsibility.

You are structured and good at prioritizing in a busy day with many parallel cases, and you keep a cool head when issues get technical or time critical. You communicate clearly and diplomatically with both customers and colleagues – on the phone, by e-mail and in person – and you're just as comfortable in a technical discussion with a developer as in a friendly, problem-solving conversation with a customer.

Practical information and application

The position is reporting to the Operations Director of TriVision A/S. You will be based in Odense, and we expect you to start in the new position as soon as possible.

For further questions regarding the role, you are welcome to contact Operations Director Torben Poulsen at 2779 5898.

We look forward to hearing from you.

TriVision delivers high-end user-friendly vision technology solutions to improve efficiency and quality in food production with reliable documentation and traceability. We focus on the food and pack industry.

jobs.occupation: Senior Infrastructure and Cloud Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

**The Opportunity

**Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. You will own the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across infrastructure, network, and workforce identity security, and rolling out the first paved roads for a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen), workforce identity and access, and drift checks for cloud configuration and network rules. You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers, and every Veo employee, work securely across our offices and clouds.

**What You Will Do

**You'll join the Security Enablement Team and focus on the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership of the team's work, pair on complex problems, and rotate responsibilities. The systems themselves stay with the owning teams, and our job is to make those teams successful.

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for our office and data center networks and the VPN that connects them, as part of the network security direction the team sets together. Day-to-day operation and firewall changes stay with the team that owns the network

• Build patterns and tooling for secure cross-site connectivity and endpoint security posture that IT can adopt and run, in a way that supports how Veo engineers actually work

• Build the patterns and automation for workforce identity and access, including SSO hygiene, MFA enforcement for employees, and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows for access to product systems, with IT owning the day-to-day operation

• Build automated checks that surface drift in cloud configuration and network rules, so the owning teams get a signal and can act on it

• Act on infrastructure and network findings from external penetration tests, routed through the team's shared intake, with the owning teams driving remediation

• Build the first version of cross-cutting capabilities, such as the cross-site VPN or the drift checks, then hand each one to a long-term owner with a written transition that covers the runbook, ownership, and escalation path

• Partner with GRC to build evidence pipelines for IT and access-related controls that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Run office hours where IT, platform, and product teams can get a network or access review

As the team matures, you'll help shape how Veo's network and identity stack evolves across our offices and clouds as the company grows.

**What You Could Bring

**This role deliberately sits where IT, cloud, and security meet. You do not need to be world class at all three. You are strong in one or two and comfortable operating across the rest.

You likely have several years of experience at that intersection. That tends to show up in several of the following:

• Solid IT fundamentals: networking, identity, endpoint posture, MFA, and SSO at production scale

• Cloud infrastructure experience: hands-on work on at least one of GCP or AWS, including IAM, networking, and basic Terraform-style IaC

• Workforce identity and access: hands-on experience with SSO and identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace) and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows

• A security mindset layered on that IT and cloud depth: you instinctively look for misconfigurations, drift, and bad access patterns, without needing to be a dedicated security specialist

• Cross-context comfort: you can work on an office network problem and a product cloud problem in the same week without context-switching pain

• Platform-as-product mindset: you've built internal tooling that real teams adopt, with guard rails built into the tools people already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured impact

• Comfort handing work back to a long-term owner once the build phase is done

• Collaboration: you work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively, and write things down.

Nice to have: VPN solutions at scale (Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, WireGuard), endpoint management tooling, and audit log pipelines.

**How We Work

**You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on most of it but not all of it, apply anyway. People who span IT, cloud, and security are rare, and we do not expect every box ticked. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI
jobs.description:
The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI.

  The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
  

  The position

  This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions.

   

  Project description

  The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment.

  The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team.

   

  Description of the scientific environment

  The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ .

  This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam

   

  Who are we looking for?

   	
• Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. 	
• Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. 	
• Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged 	
• Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities   The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems.
  

  The PhD programme

  You can undertake the PhD programme as:

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD 

  REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria:

   	
• You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; 	
• You must work on the project full-time.   Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors 	
• Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners 	
• Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues 	
• Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network 	
• Disseminate research nationally and internationally 	
• Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools

jobs.description:
**JOIN PAYCHEX EUROPE (Boilerplate text)

**At Paychex Europe, we simplify payroll, HR and workforce management for businesses across Europe. We believe great results come from people who take ownership, share knowledge, challenge the status quo and treat colleagues and customers with honesty and respect. These behaviors shape our culture and reflect the values we live by: Integrity, Respect, Partnership, Curiosity, Accountability and Service.

When you join our team, you can make a mark by helping us deliver solutions that make work easier for businesses and their employees.

**We're modernising the platform behind our rapidly growing HCM product, Emply People. As our Lead Integration Developer, you'll define the technical direction for APIs and integrations while helping evolve the platform towards a cloud-native architecture.

As a senior team member, you will be involved in hands-on coding, design, development, customization, configuration, testing, and deployment of enterprise software solutions. Additionally, you will mentor and coach colleagues while making key technical decisions, combining hands-on development with technical leadership.

Emply People is a flexible HR solution for small and medium-sized businesses, supporting the full employee journey, from recruitment and onboarding to performance, time and absence management, and offboarding.

We're transitioning to modern technologies including microservices, containerisation and serverless architectures. You'll play a key role in this transformation from an integration perspective, helping build a more scalable, efficient and agile platform.

We're looking for a Lead Developer with strong hands-on experience building enterprise-grade integrations using the .NET stack.

**What You Will Do

**Besides your daily role in Emply, you'll be part of a team of seven Lead Developers across Paychex. You'll work closely with our Architect, Product Owner/Specialist, Scrum Master, and development teams in Poland and Ukraine to design, develop, and support our browser-based product within an agile Scrum framework.

**As Lead Integration Developer, You'll Be Responsible For

**

• Defining integration architecture in collaboration with the Architect.

• Owning integration patterns and standards.

• Designing scalable APIs and integration services.

• Improving technical implementations, simplifying the codebase, and promoting coding best practices.

• Improving reliability, performance, and observability.

• Guiding the migration towards cloud-native services.

• Mentoring developers and raising engineering standards.

**What Will Help You Succeed

**We encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every single box. The following experience and skills will help you succeed in this role:

• 10+ years of proven experience designing and developing enterprise applications.

• Experience modernising legacy codebases and working with non-functional requirements such as security, performance, and scalability.

• Strong ownership of architecture and the ability to drive critical technical decisions.

• Hands-on experience with C#/.NET, MS SQL, Hangfire, REST, and GraphQL.

• Experience with API/interface modelling using OpenAPI.

• Strong understanding of integration, including enterprise integration patterns, synchronous vs. asynchronous integration, and related trade-offs.

• Experience with Domain-Driven Design (DDD).

• Experience with Git and development tools such as Azure DevOps and Jira.

• A proactive approach, with the ability to work independently and take ownership.

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts in clear business terms and act as a technical sparring partner and mentor to other developers.

• Excellent written and spoken English

**What We Offer

**In addition to Emply's incredible people and mission, we strive to foster a motivating and uplifting culture. Our offices are bright and open, with locations in Denmark and Germany. We work closely across teams and encourage a social culture, believing that working together socially makes tackling challenges more enjoyable. You will work in our Østerbro office, in a team that cares about its members and enjoys a good laugh. In short, you’ll experience plenty of learning and exciting challenges in a great work environment.

Emply is part of Paychex Europe, a leading provider of HCM solutions. Paychex Europe is growing rapidly and expanding into the European market, constantly seeking passionate talent to join them on this exciting journey. Find out more at www.emply.com.

We value different perspectives and believe diverse teams make better decisions. If this role interests you and you can see yourself contributing to our team, we encourage you to apply!

For questions about the role, please do not hesitate to contact Jacob Borella jborella@paychex.eu. Applications are reviewed continuously, and we look forward to meeting candidates who are excited about this opportunity.

Respect and partnership are at the heart of how we work together. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of age, gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, religion or background. At Paychex Europe, we strive to create an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute and thrive. Our hiring decisions are based on skills, experience and potential.

Start date: As soon as possible

Location: Østerbro (Hybrid)

Full time, 40 hours per week.

**PAYCHEX EUROPE

**Paychex Europe delivers Payroll, HR, and Workforce Management solutions that simplify processes, save time, and provide insights that help businesses support their people and drive success. Built on over 50 years of expertise, our solutions adapt to changing needs — helping businesses run more efficiently, today and tomorrow.

jobs.occupation: Senior Data & Process Specialist at Skærbæk Power Station
jobs.description:
Join us in this role where you’ll be responsible of collecting and processing data from our energy assets at Skærbæk Power Station. We’re undertaking a digitalization and modernization effort to automate, improve, and standardize our data processing to ensure high data quality. In this role regular physical visits to our locations at Avedøre Power Station and in the Gentofte office should be expected.

**Welcome to Bioenergy

**You’ll be part of Data & Application where you, together with your colleagues, will be responsible of environmental and non-financial calculations for regulatory reporting, customer settlement and internal ESG reporting for Ørsted’s Danish combined heat and power plants. We have workplaces in Skærbæk, Gentofte, and at Avedøre Power Station, and we visit our energy assets on site when needed. Data & Application is part of Digitalisation & Technology, offering a collaborative environment with passionate and skilled colleagues. As a team, we in close dialogue with colleagues across the organization. We work hybrid: daily coordination on MS Teams and workplaces in Skærbæk, other sites, or from home as needed.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• being data responsible for Skærbæk Power Station — ensuring relevant data is available for reporting and settlement

• utilizing technical insight to ensure complete, correct & validated data

• monitoring and reporting CO₂ emissions, including validating data, maintaining traceable documentation, and ensuring compliance with applicable legislation

• managing flue gas emissions data and reporting, including follow-up on emission limits, permit conditions and regulatory documentation

• participating in process optimization incl. knowledge sharing across the team.

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• possess a highly curious and analytical mindset, with a strong interest in process engineering and data reporting

• enjoy combining practical understanding of energy assets with data analysis. You hold an educational background within process-/operation and maintenance engineering, mathematics or equivalent

• strive by handling multiple tasks simultaneously with a proactively and systematically mindset and approach

• possess strong numerical skills and are persevering in finding solutions to tasks given

• strive by working both independently as well as part of a team

• need to be fluent in Danish and English both verbally and in writing due to our stakeholder landscape.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application and CV to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is DKK 45.280,- - DKK 62.260,- for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11 % contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3 % holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and well-being programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, and internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

**This position requires a background check as part of the hiring process and the offer is dependent on the outcome of this check. You will receive more information during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

jobs.occupation: System Architect (senior specialist) - Drive the architecture of next-generation medical device plat
jobs.description:
System Architect (senior specialist) – Drive the architecture of next-generation medical device platforms

This is not a software architecture role.

At Coloplast, we develop and manufacture physical medical devices used by millions of people worldwide. As a Senior System Architect, you will help define the architectural foundations of future product families and platforms, enabling innovation, scalability, and efficient product development across generations of products.

You will shape how platforms are structured to support reuse, new technology, portfolio growth, manufacturability, and long-term business value together with other R&D disciplines.

Working at the intersection of product development, manufacturing, quality, and systems engineering, you will balance user needs, product performance, regulatory requirements, risk, and platform strategy to create robust and scalable architectural solutions. Your work will ensure that future products are built on well-defined architectural foundations that enable both innovation and efficient execution.

Join a team shaping the future of R&D

You will become part of our Requirements Engineering Team within the Centre of Excellence in R&D.

The team consists of highly skilled specialists within Requirements Engineering and Systems Architecture, working with our processes and platforms.

We support development projects across the organization and continuously strengthen how systems development is conducted in a regulated medical device environment.

Design architecture that enable innovation

As our new Senior System Architect, you will be responsible for defining and maintaining system architectures related to the products and product families for one of our Chronic Care business areas, serving as the architectural lead.

Working closely with product teams and stakeholders across R&D, you will transform business needs, user needs, stakeholder requirements, and technical opportunities into architecture decisions that balance innovation, manufacturability, regulatory compliance, risk, cost, and long-term scalability.

Specifically, you will:

• 
Define and drive the platform strategy for a dedicated business area, enabling scalable product families, reusable platform assets, and accelerated delivery of future products.

• 
Drive architectural decomposition into system capabilities, subsystems, interfaces, and architectural building blocks.

• 
Establish and maintain architecture documentation and system structures.

• 
Define system boundaries, interfaces, and allocation of functionality across the system.

• 
Identify opportunities for platform reuse, standardization, modularization, and scalability.

• 
Facilitate architectural trade-offs across business, technical, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, and user perspectives.

• 
Provide architectural guidance that ensures alignment between product architecture, platform strategy, manufacturing, quality, and development activities.

• 
Support the understanding of the systems architecture discipline and the synergies to other development disciplines through close collaboration with key stakeholders across R&D and beyond

Strong architecture experience within complex product development

You combine strong systems thinking with the ability to navigate complexity and create practical solutions.

You enjoy collaborating across disciplines and are comfortable influencing decisions without having formal management responsibility. You are motivated by solving real development challenges and helping teams make sound architecture decisions. You take initiative and focus on opportunities and solutions rather than constraints.

What we expect from you:

• 5+ years of experience working with Systems Architecture, Systems Engineering, or development of complex multidisciplinary products.

• Experience defining system architecture and driving technical decisions in product development programs.

• Strong understanding of systems thinking and Systems Engineering principles.

• Experience working across multiple engineering disciplines.

• You thrive both when driving tasks independently and when working closely with colleagues to achieve shared goals

• Proven ability to influence stakeholders and create alignment across functions.

• Experience from regulated industries such as medical devices, life science, aerospace, defence, industrial automation, robotics, or similar.

• Understanding of requirements engineering, risk management, verification, and validation.

• Experience with modular architectures, platform development, and reusable solutions.

• Strong communication skills and ability to explain complex topics to a broad stakeholder audience.

• Experience defining system boundaries, interfaces, and reusable architectural building blocks that support platform-based product development.

• Motivated by both shaping long-term architectural direction and contributing to successful day-to-day product delivery.

You might also bring

• Experience from medical device development.

• Knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 14971, IEC 62304, IEC 62366, or similar standards.

• Experience with technology roadmaps and long-term architecture planning.

• Experience working with external development partners.

• Experience with architecture modelling approaches and tools.

Please note: Seniority level will be determined based on your experience (specialist or senior specialist)

Why join us?

This is a unique opportunity to influence some of Coloplast's most important development programs while helping establish platform-based development as a key capability across R&D.

You will work with highly skilled colleagues, contribute directly to products that improve people's lives, and play a vital role in enabling future innovation through strong system architecture.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about this position, please contact Head of Requirement Engineering, Centre of Excellence, R&D, Stine Renberg at +45 49113320. We continuously review applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.
